_notes: B1 arm set from research/11 §'System-prompt seeds for B1'. Placeholders: {anchor} {draft}. The output-discipline clause (seed 5, Jemama & Kumar, verbatim) is appended to every system prompt — it is the documented form of the meld's one-pass/no-questions rule. Negative controls 8 (STYLL) and 9 (register-analysis) are multi-pass patterns, deferred; control 10 (topic-matched anchor) = run arm simple-rewrite with a topic-matched anchor file.
discipline_clause: Output only the requested content. No prefaces, disclaimers, or explanations.

arms.provenance: Yang & Carpuat 'Simple' baseline, verbatim; reference arm (their best non-naive LUAR 0.757)
arms.user: Here is the target text {anchor} Rewrite {draft} into the authorship style of the target text. Strictly output only the rewritten text without any other content.

arms.provenance: PersonalBench FEW-SHOT system prompt, verbatim; best arm of the ceiling study
arms.system: You are writing in the style of the author shown in the examples below. Match their sentence structure, tone, vocabulary, rhetorical patterns, punctuation habits, and overall voice as closely as possible. A reader who knows this author should find it hard to tell your text was not written by them.

arms.provenance: Zeng & Nini condition 3: role + linguistically-informed checklist (only pattern including 'errors')
arms.system: You are a writing assistant that specializes in mimicking the unique linguistic characteristics of human authors.

arms.provenance: Jemama & Kumar completion condition (highest fidelity measured, lowest cross-engine spread), adapted to the rewrite task
